memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Kohathite clans were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle. The number of all the males a month old or more was 8,600. The Kohathites were responsible for the care of the sanctuary. The leader of the families of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel. They were responsible for the care of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the articles of the sanctuary used in ministering, the curtain, and everything related to their use. - Num 3:27-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Kohathites were given the most sacred duty of all: caring for the holy furnishings — the ark, the table, the lampstand, and the altars. These were the objects that stood at the very heart of Israel's worship. Handling them was a high honour and a serious responsibility.

Yet even the Kohathites, entrusted with such holy things, still had to follow God's instructions carefully. Later in Numbers we learn they were not even to touch the holy objects directly, but to carry them in the prescribed way. Great privilege came with great care.

There is wisdom here for us. The closer we come to holy things — to leadership in God's work, to teaching His word, to handling sacred responsibilities — the more carefully we must walk. Privilege is never a licence for carelessness.

At the same time, God trusted the Kohathites with His most precious things. He entrusts His people with precious things too: His word, His gospel, His church, the souls of others. The apostle Paul spoke of being "entrusted with the gospel" (1 Thess 2:4).

Handle what God has entrusted to you with reverence and care today. Whether it is His truth, your family, or those you serve — these are holy trusts from His hand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What holy things has God entrusted to your care?
- Do you handle God's word and work with reverence?
- How can you be more careful and faithful with sacred trusts?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for entrusting precious things to me. Help me to handle Your word, Your work, and Your people with reverence and care. Amen.
